messages:
Priya S.: morning team :wave: I'm taking primary for the next 8h (UTC). Quick handoff: primary=Priya, secondary=Marco. There's a small coverage gap we need to watch around 02:00-03:00 UTC — that's when infra scheduled snapshot job runs and we've seen tail latencies before.

Marco L.: noted. I'll be on standby for those hours. do we have runbook links handy?

Priya S.: yes — pinned below. TL;DR pointers first: 1) If 5xx spike: check model pool saturation, fallback to smaller variant (model-v1-small). 2) If KV cache misses spike: restart cache service on the node reported in metrics (see runbook). 3) If API gateway 504s: check the scaling group + recent deploys.

Jules K.: adding: if user-facing errors > 5% for >5m, enable canary fallback policy (route to hosted-backup) and alert PG. Use the circuit-breaker route in the console.

Rotation Bot: scheduled handoff: Priya S. -> Marco L. at 2026-03-14T08:00:00Z. Reminder: runbook review required.

SRE Bot: INCIDENT NOTICE :rotating_light: 1812350001 - Increased 503 rate on /v1/generate (prod-us-east-1). Affected: 3.2% of requests in last 2m. Pager sent to oncall-primary.

Priya S.: Ack incident notice. Marco can you pick initial triage? I'll start validating customer impact.

Marco L.: I'm on it. First checks: 1) tail logs on inference-*-us-east-1 for 503s 2) check autoscaler events 3) check Redis/KV error counts. Trying logs now.

Marco L.: found a pattern: a subset of requests hitting model-pool-a are returning 503s with error 'model-oom' in the logs. Affected nodes: gpua-03, gpua-07.

Priya S.: thanks. Quick mitigation: scale down batch size and roll traffic to model-v1-small. Steps: open console -> routes -> add policy fallback to model-v1-small. If rollout fails, manually set `MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=512` on pool.

Jules K.: linking runbooks and quick commands:
- Model pool OOM runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-pool-oom
- API gateway 5xx triage: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/api-5xx-triage
- KV cache restart: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-restart

Quick command to reduce batch size (kubectl exec example):
```
kubectl -n inference exec deploy/pool-controller -- /bin/sh -c "env | grep BATCH || true"
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/pool-controller MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=512
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/pool-controller
```
If you need to drain a GPU node:
```
kubectl cordon gpua-07
kubectl drain gpua-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Marco L.: applied fallback route to model-v1-small, traffic shifted. Observing metrics... 503 rate falling.

SRE Bot: METRICS UPDATE 3m after mitigation - 503 rate decreased to 0.6%. Latency stable.

Priya S.: excellent. Customer impact assessment: affected a small fraction of traffic; no major accounts reported errors yet. I'm drafting an incident notification to CSMs in case.

Marco L.: left a note in the model-pool-oom runbook: gpua-03/07 showed repeated OOMs likely due to recent weight-quant job. Recommend reverting quant stage for those nodes until we confirm config.

Jules K.: reminder for handoff checklist: - confirm mitigation active - escalate to infra if nodes repeatedly OOM - verify alerts silenced for noisy alarms - record timeline in incident doc (link below).

Priya S.: incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1812350001 (creating). Timeline so far will go in that doc.

Rotation Bot: handoff reminder in 30m.

Marco L.: I'll keep monitoring through the gap. If things look stable in 45m, we can mark incident as mitigated and continue with normal handoff.

Priya S.: for the next oncall please note these quick pointers (copy into your notes):
- Runbook shortcuts: model-pool-oom, api-5xx-triage, kv-cache-restart.
- Fast mitigations: fallback route to smaller model, reduce MAX_BATCH_TOKENS, cordon/drain bad GPU node.
- When to escalate to infra: persistent OOMs on >2 nodes or hardware errors in telemetry.
- Customer comms: only if affected >10% traffic or any enterprise SLA customer reports errors.

Jules K.: also add: check console -> per-route token cost chart to ensure fallback doesn't explode spend.

SRE Bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Next update scheduled in 30m.

Priya S.: Handing over to Marco in 20m. Marco, confirm you have the runbook links and the playbook in your notes.

Marco L.: Confirmed. I have runbooks, incident doc, and will escalate to infra if gpua nodes continue failing. Taking primary at T+20.

Priya S.: thanks team :thumbsup: leaving notes in the incident doc and pinning runbook links in the channel. Handoff complete at 1812353600.
